text:
Amanda: quick readout from the smoke scan of meridianX-13B int6 — cost wins but a couple of signal weirdnesses on longform prompts
Tariq: can you share the high-level numbers? latency / $ / quality delta?
Amanda: sure — baseline (13B fp16) -> int6: token cost ~ -37%, p95 latency +5% (due to kv-cache behavior), QA F1 on longform summarization slice dropped ~4.2 pts
Evan: 4.2 pts is notable. which slice? long narratives or multi-doc?
Amanda: multi-doc long narratives (avg chunked length ~1.6k tokens). short chat / search snippets look fine, dev bench shows negligible regressions
Maria: do we have unit-econ per 1k tokens? helps product figure tradeoffs
Amanda: unit price (hosted) baseline ~ $0.018 / 1k; int6 ~ $0.011 / 1k — saves ~$7k/mo at current traffic for the pilot route
Sophia: is the quality drop concentrated on a small set of prompts or broad?
Amanda: preliminary slicing indicates concentrated on prompts with heavy entity co-reference and table-like content. sample failure attached in thread (I'll paste below)
Amanda: ```
INPUT: long doc with repeating entity aliases...
BASELINE OUTPUT: accurate co-ref resolution across docs
INT6 OUTPUT: occasional entity swaps, hallucinated aggregation of rows
```
Tariq: could this be priming sensitivity + quantization interaction? we saw similar with zephyr int4 earlier
Evan: maybe kv-cache truncation + subtle fp rounding on attention logits. can we repro with seq_len=2048 local run and compare logits?
Amanda: yes running a debug trace now. early signal: softmax tails slightly shifted for tokens at boundaries
Maria: from product POV: if it's limited to <5% of traffic and cost savings are 40%, might be worth routing heuristics + fallback. propose: route 95% -> int6, 5% -> fp16 for longform or flagged slices
Sophia: prefer an automated routing rule rather than manual split. something like: if prompt_length>1200 OR has_table=true -> fp16
Tariq: +1. can we implement a quick feature-flagged routing rule? e.g. in routing DSL:```
route {
  condition: prompt_length > 1200 || contains_table
  model: meridianX-13B-fp16
  fallback: meridianX-13B-int6
  sample_rate: 1.0
}
default: meridianX-13B-int6
```
Amanda: I pushed a canary rule in staging under flag `meridianx-longform-fp16`
deploy-bot: Canary routing rule meridianx-longform-fp16 deployed to staging at 2026-03-23T15:12:10Z :rocket:
Evan: let's also add a lightweight scorecard metric: longform-coherence (binary pass/fail on 500 evals) and track unit-econ delta per route
Maria: agree. product wants a clear threshold: if coherence drop > 3 pts at 10k sample we rollback
Sophia: ops question: does using fp16 for the longform route change capacity planning? we need dedicated headroom for fp16 fallbacks
Tariq: capacity hit is small at 5% traffic, but we should pre-warm instances and set autoscale min=2 for that route
Amanda: noted. I'll update canary config with autoscale_min and alerting on p95 latency bump >12%
Amanda: next steps I propose: 1) run a 10k longform eval (GTN slice) comparing fp16 vs int6 on coherence/recall 2) run token-level econ projection for 30/60/90 day traffic curves 3) implement routing rule in prod behind flag and monitor scorecard
Evan: happy to run the 10k eval — will need the labeled GTN slice + eval harness path
Amanda: GTN slice shared: s3://redwood-eval/meridianx/longform-coherence/10k.jsonl
Maria: product will validate the user impact and confirm acceptable loss threshold; FYI we'll propose a 90/10 rollout if results look good
Sophia: can we add logging tag to each routed response: "route_variant" to compute weighted unit-econ easily?
Tariq: good call. include tag and cost metadata on traces
Amanda: agreed. I'll add logs + scorecard dashboard (coherence, recall, lat p95, unit_cost). will post dashboard link when ready
Amanda: quick Q — anyone object to proceeding with the canary + 10k eval?
Evan: no objections, go ahead
Maria: go for it, product supports the plan
Sophia: +1 from devex, will help with routing DSL tests
Tariq: I'll watch the canary and jump on pager if latency spikes
Amanda: thanks all — I'll follow up with results and a recommended routing percentage after evals. :thumbsup:
